l.i: rgo queri abfentes, mi Lecti, define Musas,
Ecce tuo à Beza quas petis, intus habes.
Unde haec atra maris facies? tanta unde pro-
cella?
Et pro caeruleo spuma colore tumens?
Hispanum Vasto nunc gurgite mergitur agmen,
Et vix submersos aequoris unda capit:
Sic Pharao comitissa petens sacra agmina Mosi,
Factus Erythrei piscibus esca maris:
Festis Sterque Dei sanctorum et gentis Sterque:
Curribus hic multis, navibus ille potens:
Exitio currus navesque feruntur eodem,
Sanguinis Sut sanet purior unda sitim:
Et regredi ut posset (quoniam est aggressor Sterque)
Neutri commoti Numinis ira dedit:
Sed quorsum Hispanus terrenis feruidus astu,
Ad Boream et nivibus littora cana fugit?
Nempe iubente Deo, totum fitientis ut orbem,
Ardorem gelidis temperet Arctos aquis.
Quinetiam ardenti medius occurrit in Sndis,
Non minus ardescens alter et ille Draco:
Iste quidem patriae succensus amore tuendae,
Ille Anglas sitiens totus auarus opes.

page.notes: Several words in the verse are hard to read in the scan: "Sterque", "Sndis", "Sut", "Festis" and "Hispanum Vasto" are doubtful and may be misprinted or long-s/ligature forms (the Greek/Latin ligature "Ꝺ"-type forms in "Unde" and "Vnda" are rendered as printed). Lines with initial capital letters are set as ornamental initials; the page's first verse fragment is a continuation from the previous page.
